sheet-67-1.description: The bottom strip of sheet 67, below the title and the town key map, shows the bay front of Stone Harbor along Great Channel from the Stone Harbor Yacht Club to 83rd Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Sunset Drive runs along the channel behind a row of bay-front lots in blocks 90, 86 and 83, curving at its west end around the yacht club grounds into Snug Harbor. The Stone Harbor Yacht Club (with a note that it is closed in winter, electric lights and a range in the kitchen) stands at the point, and the bulkhead is lined with private boat docks. Bay-front dwellings, an open shed, garages and a boat house face the channel between the yacht club and 86th Street; the blocks on the other side of Sunset Drive (88, 87, 86 and 84) show only their first rows of lots, continuing on sheet 100. South Basin cuts into the bulkhead between 86th Street and 84th Street, and beyond it a separate stretch of bulkhead with a few dwellings in block 83 lies at 84th Street. Cross streets 89th to 84th Street are drawn 60 feet wide, running from Sunset Drive to the bottom edge of the sheet.
notes: Stone Harbor Yacht Club at the west end of Sunset Drive.
Placed from four Sunset Drive junctions along one line (helmert); the scale and rotation agree with sheets 68 and 100.

Title page with town key map (small scale, masked out) plus two map areas: bottom strip at 100 ft (Sunset Drive along Great Channel from the Yacht Club to 86th St, and a block at 84th St / Sunset Drive east of South Basin) and a top-right inset at 50 ft of the Stone Harbor Pier (auditorium on piles) off the Boardwalk at 106th St. Printed 'New Sheet Aug. 1917'. Key map: skip area (not configured).

sheet-67-2.description: A framed inset in the top right corner of sheet 67, drawn at the larger scale of 50 feet to an inch, shows the Stone Harbor Pier, which runs out into the Atlantic Ocean from the Boardwalk at the end of 106th Street. At the landward end, on the Boardwalk, is the restaurant building drawn on sheet 103 (its block number is printed on it). The pier is built on piles: a front range of four one-storey stores lettered A to D flanks a two-storey entrance, behind which the long auditorium hall, with a balcony across its landward end, extends to a one-storey extension and a separate small building at the seaward end. The auditorium has electric lights, no heat and no fire apparatus. The pier stands inside a dashed outline that marks its piling, with open water on both sides. 106th Street, 60 feet wide, appears only as its last few feet at the top left corner of the inset.
notes: Stone Harbor Pier, auditorium built on piles, lights electric, no heat, no fire apparatus.
Placed from four points carried from sheet 103 part 1 (corners of the pier outline at the Boardwalk and of the restaurant on piles), all within about 110 ft; low confidence.

sheet-68-1.description: The upper half of sheet 68 covers New Stone Harbor between 94th Street and 87th Street, from the edge of the blocks beyond 2nd Avenue (lots 71 to 80, drawn only in part along the top of the sheet) across 2nd Avenue and 1st Avenue to the line marked Proposed Board Walk, with the Atlantic Ocean beyond. The heavy line below it separates the lower part of the sheet, which continues the same avenues from 87th Street to 80th Street. 2nd Avenue is drawn 120 feet wide with the single track of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad down it, and an open platform and railroad station near 87th Street. 1st Avenue is 70 feet wide and the cross streets 60 feet. The blocks, numbered 87 to 93 to match the street numbers, are laid out in uniform narrow building lots, numbered in sequence, with a row of shallow lots 1 to 8 along the ocean front. The district was barely built in 1917: a few dwellings, among them a two-and-a-half-storey house with outbuildings near 90th Street, a plastered outbuilding, a dwelling on 91st Street with a note that a frame dwelling is to be built here, and Italian quarters and an office in block 88 near 89th Street, which were probably workmen's lodgings for the development. Most lots are empty. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch with the compass rose on the dividing line between the two halves.
notes: The proposed boardwalk along the ocean front is drawn as a dashed line; the area is now built up well seaward of it.
The railroad in 2nd Avenue (W.J. & S.R.R.) is gone; 2nd Avenue is the town's main road.

New Stone Harbor, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (upper) 94th to 87th St between 2nd Av (WJ&SR railroad) and 1st Av; part 2 (lower) 87th to 80th St between 2nd Av and the proposed Boardwalk.

sheet-68-2.description: The lower half of sheet 68 continues New Stone Harbor north-east from 87th Street to 80th Street, from the edge of the blocks beyond 2nd Avenue across 2nd Avenue and 1st Avenue to the proposed boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean. 2nd Avenue, 120 feet wide, carries the single track of the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad; 1st Avenue is 70 feet wide and the cross streets 60 feet. Blocks 80 to 86 are divided into uniform narrow building lots, with shallow ocean-front lots 1 to 8 below 1st Avenue. The largest building is the Harbor Inn in block 83 between 84th Street and 83rd Street, with a windmill, an elevated water tank and a second tank beside it. A pavilion with a row of small bath houses stands at the ocean end of block 82, and scattered dwellings and bungalows, a boarding house, a garage, a stable and a contractor's shanty are drawn near 80th to 84th Street. The rest of the lots are vacant. The sheet's scale bar (100 feet to one inch) is printed in 1st Avenue between 82nd Street and 80th Street, and a heavy line with the compass rose separates this half from the upper half of the sheet.
notes: Harbor Inn, block 83, with windmill and elevated tank.
Pavilion and bath houses at the ocean end of block 82.
Few 1st Avenue junctions north of 83rd Street are in OpenStreetMap; the part is placed mainly from 2nd Avenue junctions.

New Stone Harbor, 100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (upper) 94th to 87th St between 2nd Av (WJ&SR railroad) and 1st Av; part 2 (lower) 87th to 80th St between 2nd Av and the proposed Boardwalk.

sheet-100-1.description: The upper part of sheet 100 covers the centre of Stone Harbor in 1917, from 97th Street to 90th Street and from the bulkheads of Shelter Haven and Snug Harbor across 3rd Avenue to 2nd Avenue. It holds most of the town's public buildings. At the Shelter Haven end of 96th Street stand the Shelter Haven Hotel, a garage with the fire department (auto combination hose and ladder) and stores. The Reading railroad (A.C.R.R., Reading) runs down 96th Street to the Stone Harbor Water Co. works at 2nd Avenue, with its pumping station, cistern and standpipe beside the Stone Harbor Electric Light and Power Co. plant and garage in block 95. Along 96th Street and 95th Street are stores, a post office, a lumber office and the telephone exchange; there is an Episcopal church on 3rd Avenue in block 94, a public school and public school kindergarten in block 93 near 94th Street, and a Lutheran church on 3rd Avenue at 93rd Street. Dwellings are scattered through the blocks, thickest near Shelter Haven, and the blocks north-east of 92nd Street, beside Snug Harbor, are nearly empty. Blocks 90 to 96 are divided into narrow building lots, some lettered A to S where they were resurveyed. Water pipes (8 inch and 6 inch) are drawn in 2nd Avenue and 94th Street. A heavy line along 2nd Avenue separates this part from the lower part of the sheet; the part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Shelter Haven Hotel at the bay end of 96th Street.
Stone Harbor Water Co. and Stone Harbor Elec. Light & Power Co. in block 95 at 2nd Avenue.
The Reading branch (A.C.R.R.) in 96th Street and the W.J. & S.R.R. in 2nd Avenue are gone.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (upper) 96th to 90th St, Shelter Haven / Snug Harbor to 2nd Av (fire dept, Shelter Haven Hotel, water works, school); part 2 (lower) 90th to 83rd St between Snug Harbor / South Basin bulkheads and 2nd Av.

sheet-100-2.description: The lower part of sheet 100 covers Stone Harbor from 90th Street to 83rd Street between 3rd Avenue and 2nd Avenue, with a strip of the bay-side blocks beyond 3rd Avenue that end at the bulkheads of Snug Harbor and South Basin. South Basin, numbered as block 84, is a rectangular boat basin cut into the blocks between 86th Street and 84th Street, with a small dock at its head; the bay-side lots further along are drawn on sheet 67. Below 3rd Avenue the blocks 83 to 89 are divided into uniform narrow lots, many lettered A to U. The district is residential and thinly built: scattered dwellings, a few auto sheds, the Ellsworth hotel at 90th Street and 3rd Avenue, a boarding house and stores near 88th Street on 2nd Avenue, and a fire department house (combination hose and ladder truck) in block 85 on 86th Street. Block 84 between 85th Street and 84th Street has a row of about a dozen small identical dwellings. 2nd Avenue, along the bottom of the part, carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, and a 6 inch water pipe runs in 83rd Street. The sheet's scale bar (100 feet to one inch) is printed in 3rd Avenue at South Basin, and a heavy line with the compass rose separates this part from the upper part of the sheet.
notes: Fire department house in block 85.

100 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line: part 1 (upper) 96th to 90th St, Shelter Haven / Snug Harbor to 2nd Av (fire dept, Shelter Haven Hotel, water works, school); part 2 (lower) 90th to 83rd St between Snug Harbor / South Basin bulkheads and 2nd Av.

sheet-101-1.description: The main part of sheet 101 covers the lagoon development on the bay side of Stone Harbor between 96th Street and 105th Street, laid out in 1917 as fingers of building lots between dredged waterways and still almost empty. A strip of ordinary blocks (99 to 104) along 3rd Avenue forms the right edge. To the left, Sunset Drive loops from the bay end of 96th Street around Shelter Haven, past block 98, and runs down the Great Channel side to a turning circle at Berkley Road; Corinthian Drive and 101st Street cross the block between them. A long, curving finger of lots on Sunset Drive (block 200) runs around Stone Harbor, a basin lettered in the middle of the sheet, and back to 104th Street, which crosses the outlet of the basin on a bridge. Below 104th Street the fingers between Great Channel, Pleasure Bay and Carnival Bay begin, carrying Golden Gate Road, Sunset Drive and Corinthian Drive (blocks 201 to 203, 104), with match lines A-B and C-D where they continue in the two framed insets on the left of the sheet. Lots are numbered in long sequences up to the 500s; bulkheads with outer dashed lines edge every waterway. Only about thirty dwellings are drawn, some with boat landings, and a colonial apartments building on Sunset Drive. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: '3rd' at the right edge is 3rd Avenue, its suffix cut off by the sheet edge.
The 1917 Sunset Drive along the east side of the Stone Harbor basin is today's Sunrise Drive; it was left out of the control because its modern line runs about 20 m west of the drawn one.
101st Street between Sunset Drive and Corinthian Drive is today's Charles Street.
Golden Gate Road is today's Golden Gate Drive.
Fitted scale is about 4 percent larger across the sheet than along 3rd Avenue: the lagoon streets are drawn closer to 3rd Avenue than their modern lines.

100 ft. Bay-side lagoon district: main part with Sunset Drive, Corinthian Drive, Berkley Road, 99th to 104th St around Stone Harbor (basin); two framed insets on the left: Corinthian Pl finger (top) and Golden Gate Road finger (bottom).

sheet-101-2.description: A framed inset in the top left corner of sheet 101 continues the finger of lots between Pleasure Bay and Carnival Bay south of match line A-B at the bottom of the main part. Corinthian Place, 100 feet wide, runs down the middle of the finger to a turning circle at its tip, with block 202 on both sides: lots 18 to 46 on the Carnival Bay side and 51 to 81 on the Pleasure Bay side, each running back to the bulkhead. The finger is almost empty in 1917: a few dwellings, among them a stuccoed house, with a boat landing and an auto shed on the Pleasure Bay side and a dwelling near the tip. The inset is drawn at the main part's scale of 100 feet to an inch and turned the same way, but shifted on the page to fit; it was placed by the match line alone.
notes: Placed from one point carried from part 1 at match line A-B, with the scale and north of part 1; low confidence.
Corinthian Place does not appear under that name in OpenStreetMap.

100 ft. Bay-side lagoon district: main part with Sunset Drive, Corinthian Drive, Berkley Road, 99th to 104th St around Stone Harbor (basin); two framed insets on the left: Corinthian Pl finger (top) and Golden Gate Road finger (bottom).

sheet-101-3.description: A framed inset on the lower left of sheet 101 continues the Golden Gate Road finger between Great Channel and Pleasure Bay south of match line C-D at the bottom of the main part. Golden Gate Road, 80 feet wide, runs down the middle of block 201 to a turning circle at the tip, with lots 26 to 89 numbered round the finger and running back to the bulkheads on both sides. In 1917 only two dwellings with a boat landing on Pleasure Bay are drawn. The inset is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned the same way as the main part, but shifted on the page; it was placed by the match line alone.
notes: Placed from one point carried from part 1 at match line C-D, with the scale and north of part 1; low confidence.
Golden Gate Road is today's Golden Gate Drive.

100 ft. Bay-side lagoon district: main part with Sunset Drive, Corinthian Drive, Berkley Road, 99th to 104th St around Stone Harbor (basin); two framed insets on the left: Corinthian Pl finger (top) and Golden Gate Road finger (bottom).

sheet-102.description: Sheet 102 covers the south-western blocks of Stone Harbor from 97th Street to 105th Street, from 3rd Avenue across 2nd Avenue and 1st Avenue to the bulkhead, the Boardwalk and the Atlantic Ocean. 2nd Avenue, 120 feet wide, carries the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad (Penna. Lines); the cross streets are 60 feet and 3rd Avenue and 1st Avenue 70 feet wide. Each block is divided into narrow building lots, numbered or lettered, with short rows of ocean-front lots 1 to 8 between 1st Avenue and the bulkhead. Building is sparse. The largest buildings are a hotel with stores and a billiard room on 3rd Avenue at 97th Street, a Roman Catholic church on 3rd Avenue at 99th Street, and on the ocean front a casino and moving picture theater built on piles at the end of 98th Street and bath houses built on piles near 103rd Street. A jetty runs out into the ocean at 104th Street. The rest are scattered dwellings, a small store and auto sheds. Water pipes (6 inch and 8 inch) are drawn in 98th, 99th and 102nd Street and in 2nd Avenue and 3rd Avenue. Along the bottom the sheet reaches the ends of Chelsea Place, a short loop street between the avenues at 105th Street drawn in full on sheet 103. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with its scale bar on the ocean front.
notes: Casino and moving picture theater built on piles at the ocean end of 98th Street.
R.C. church on 3rd Avenue at 99th Street.
A jetty into the ocean at 104th Street.
100 ft, single part: 97th to 105th St from 3rd Av to the Boardwalk (2nd Av with WJ&SR railroad, 1st Av, casino moving picture theater on piles, jetty). Pilot sheet.

sheet-103-1.description: The main part of sheet 103 covers the southern end of Stone Harbor in 1917, from 112th Street to 106th Street and the edge of block 105, between the bulkhead on Carnival Bay and the Atlantic Ocean. Sunset Drive runs diagonally along the bay front at the top, with a row of narrow bay-front lots in block 107 behind the bulkhead; below it 3rd Avenue, 2nd Avenue (120 feet, with the West Jersey and Seashore Railroad, Penna. R.R.) and 1st Avenue cross the sheet. Blocks 112 and 111 are still undivided, and the cross streets between 2nd Avenue and 1st Avenue from 112th to 108th Street are marked Not Opened, as is 1st Avenue west of 108th Street. The one built-up area is blocks 108 to 110 between 3rd Avenue and 2nd Avenue, filled with rows of small, identical dwellings on narrow lots lettered and numbered in sequence, a development of about a hundred cottages with a boarding house at 3rd Avenue. Elsewhere there are only a few dwellings. Chelsea Place, a narrow loop street with a planted centre, runs through block 105 between 3rd Avenue and 1st Avenue. At the ocean end of 106th Street a restaurant built on piles stands on the bulkhead and Boardwalk, at the landward end of the Stone Harbor Pier drawn on sheet 67. Water pipes of 4 to 8 inches are drawn along most streets. A small framed inset in the top right corner (not part of this area) and the lower-left part of the sheet are separated from it by heavy lines.
notes: Blocks 108 to 110 between 3rd and 2nd Avenue hold rows of small identical dwellings.
Cross streets 108th to 112th between 2nd and 1st Avenue and 1st Avenue west of 108th Street marked Not Opened.
Restaurant built on piles at the Boardwalk, 106th Street, at the head of the Stone Harbor Pier (sheet 67).

100 ft. Main part 112th to 105th St from Sunset Drive / Carnival Bay to 1st Av and the Boardwalk (Chelsea Pl); lower-left part split by a heavy line: Sunset Drive along Great Channel 96th to 92nd St with Shelter Haven; small framed inset top right (block 105 at 3rd Av on Carnival Bay).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: framed inset top right: lots 140 to 142 of block 105 (boat and auto house) at 3rd Av on Carnival Bay (no street junction; a three-lot fragment beyond the edge of part 1; needs carried points from sheet-103-1 (lot lines of block 105 at 3rd Av)).

sheet-103-2.description: The lower-left part of sheet 103, separated from the main part by a heavy line, covers the bay front of central Stone Harbor between 96th Street and 92nd Street, where Sunset Drive runs diagonally along the bulkhead of Great Channel. Shelter Haven, a basin, lies along the left edge, and Snug Harbor at the right. The Reading railroad (A.C.R.R.) comes down 96th Street on a bridge to a freight house at the channel. Along the bulkhead are boat docks at 96th, 95th and 94th Street, a fish house and the Channel Apartments at 94th Street. Behind Sunset Drive the blocks 92 to 96 are divided into narrow lots, with scattered dwellings, a moving picture theatre on 96th Street, a plumber's shop and a few stores along the Shelter Haven side of block 96. The lots continue across the bottom of the sheet into the blocks drawn on sheet 100. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, the scale bar lying in Great Channel.
notes: Railroad freight house at the channel end of 96th Street.
Placed from Sunset Drive junctions only, which lie along one line.

100 ft. Main part 112th to 105th St from Sunset Drive / Carnival Bay to 1st Av and the Boardwalk (Chelsea Pl); lower-left part split by a heavy line: Sunset Drive along Great Channel 96th to 92nd St with Shelter Haven; small framed inset top right (block 105 at 3rd Av on Carnival Bay).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: framed inset top right: lots 140 to 142 of block 105 (boat and auto house) at 3rd Av on Carnival Bay (no street junction; a three-lot fragment beyond the edge of part 1; needs carried points from sheet-103-1 (lot lines of block 105 at 3rd Av)).
